regions.merged_text: I do hope that things are brightening or soon to brighten up for you and your lately so bereaved family. I have just finished a letter to the widow of the late A. J. Crawford, whose husband - same A.J. - was one time the fond hope of a fervently loving Catholic mother, but alas! for human fickleness! as my futile efforts to bring him back to appreciation of religion proved in his case. Alas for so many whose promisning youth has sadly ripened into disapoint- ing maturity and senile disaster. No doubt David, the Royal Prophet; forsaw the possibility of the defec- tion of Solomon's eldest brother, had (he) lived when, having stormed Heaven with all kinds of prayers and penance that the boy might be spared him, he was nevertheless taken, he washed himself from his penance and tears to the surprise of and edifycation of his contemporaries as well as future gener- ations even to this end of time, - faithful and humble and real philosopher that he was. . Ha! but such resignation to such berevements never fail to multiply the graces of the one so tried - in reality the priviliged one, could we but peer through the vail of only the temporal - to say nothing of the eternal - future. From a sinner and an adulterer, to which David had in a moment of weakness fallen, through resignation to this and other trials perhaps more heartrending, he becomes the outstanding seer of penance, - the Royal Prophet and Psalmist, "a man according to God's own heart," nay, an outstanding progenetor of the Hope of all ages the God-Man Himself Jesus Christ our Redeemer and Saviour! What are our trials, severe as they seem, when we think of Abraham offering his only son Isaac? To say that he became "The father of all the faithful", is only to touch, as it were, on the visible. Who can doubt that before he left the Mountain, God has given him a picture of the Kingdom of Heaven in the Church and the coming generations to the blending of time into the incomprehensible glory of eternity?
